title.title: Elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields are modular
title.subtitle: Claim: each $E/K$ matches an automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over $K$, at every place

object.heading: Prime switching: congruences down to a curve already known to be modular

nodes.label: a curve known to be modular

beats.text: Each link is a Jacobian of a cyclic cover, chosen so existing lifting theorems apply
Modularity passes up the chain, as in Wiles's 3–5 switch
One unmet hypothesis, at 2, 3 or $p$, would break the chain

achievement.label: Modularity over imaginary quadratic fields
statement: L(E/K, s) = L(\pi_E, s - \tfrac{1}{2})\ \text{ for every } E/K
achievement.context: Before: all curves over $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ and a few small fields (Caraiani–Newton 2023), a positive proportion elsewhere
achievement.note: Only 30 pages, with the big lifting theorems used as black boxes

verify.ourCheck: We read the main theorem and caveats; nothing was checked independently

sources.quote: Every elliptic curve E over every imaginary quadratic field K is modular

Caraiani-Newton (2023, arXiv:2301.10509) modularity of all elliptic curves over many imaginary quadratic fields, including Q(i) and a few other small fields, and a positive proportion of curves more generally

Only 30 pages for a statement whose previous partial cases needed the ten-author potential automorphy machinery; it relies on those modularity lifting theorems (Calegari-Geraghty patching, ACC+ results, Caraiani-Newton) as black boxes
every hypothesis of those theorems (residual image, local conditions at 2, 3, p) must be met, which is exactly where such arguments fail

sources.ref: article, Modularity over imaginary quadratic fields (family 030)
sources.quote: It is a prime-switching argument in the spirit of Wiles's 3–5 switch: Jacobians of cyclic covers whose cohomology links $E$ through congruences mod $p$, mod 3, mod $p$ to a curve already known to be modular
read each family's summary and abstracts and the introduction and main theorem of every principal paper

plain: Every elliptic curve over these number systems matches a modular form, like a fingerprint on file

steps: Link the curve to others by congruences, one prime at a time
Switch primes: mod $p$, then mod $3$, then mod $p$ again
End at a curve already known to be modular

voice.text: Congruences chain the curve down to one known to be modular, as in Wiles's switch.
Switch primes: mod p, mod three, mod p, landing on a known modular curve.
Claimed: every elliptic curve is modular.
